sentences.text: Paranthodon africanus was a thyreophoran stegosaurian dinosaur that lived approximately 145 to 140 million years ago during the Berriasian and Valanginian stages of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Africa.
This animal possessed an elongated snout that was convex on top, though the curve was not extreme.
It was set apart from other members of its group by a long and wide rear extension of the premaxilla bone, maxillary teeth featuring a very large cingulum, and prominent crests on the tooth crowns.

Descriptions of the creature vary, with one source noting it had plates measuring about 4 meters long and 1.8 meters high, while another estimated the total length at 5.0 meters and the weight between 454 and 907 kilograms.

Paranthodon was discovered in 1845 and was one of the first stegosaurians ever found, with amateur geologists William Guybon Atherstone and Andrew Geddes Bain locating fossils near Dassieklip in the Bushman's River Valley.

British paleontologist Richard Owen initially misidentified the fossil fragments as belonging to the pareiasaur Anthodon, a conclusion later challenged by Broom who suggested Owen had mixed the skull, teeth, and partially distorted jaw of a pareiasaur with the partial upper jaw of a dinosaur from two different species.
The genus Paranthodon was eventually named by Nopcsa in 1929.
The holotype of Paranthodon was found in the upper part of the Kirkwood Formation in the Cape Province, South Africa.

Franz Nopcsa classified Paranthodon as a stegosaurid in 1929, a classification supported by most modern studies which currently place it as a stegosaurid related to Stegosaurus, Tuojiangosaurus, and Loricatosaurus.
Initially, the fossils now known as Paranthodon were classified as ankylosaurians by Broom, who first assigned the name Palaeoscincus africanus to the material.
Paranthodon is considered to belong to the family Stegosauridae, being a close relative of Kentrosaurus, within the subfamily Stegosaurinae, making the parent group of Paranthodon Stegosauridae.

The holotype specimen BMNH 47338 was found in the Kirkwood Formation, dated to the Berriasian and early Valanginian ages, and Paranthodon was the first species uncovered in this formation in South Africa.

Teeth found at the 151-million-year-old Mugher locality in southern and eastern Africa may extend Paranthodon's known age and range, suggesting its geographic distribution extends significantly if these teeth are correctly attributed to the genus.

A 2018 review found no diagnostic stegosaurian features in Paranthodon, though it was still referred to Stegosauria based on similarity and phylogenetic analysis, while a 1981 review using modern taxonomic techniques confirmed Paranthodon as a valid genus of stegosaurid. It is debated whether the type material of Paranthodon actually bears synapomorphies of Stegosauria, despite phylogenetic analyses placing it within the group.
